liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (5 reviews): Cryptical into The Other One is called worth the download alone, with Jerry playing relentlessly; Garcia's guitar in the opening five minutes of The Other One is described as intensely psychedelic [6][7][8][9][10]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (2 reviews): Cryptical reprise sounds primal, with Phil possibly hinting at New Potato or 13s; The late show begins with Cryptical Envelopment [5][13]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Dark Star is intense and brooding [14]
- **William Tell Bridge** (1 review): William Tell Bridge is singled out as a rarity [5]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): This Eleven is full of tension [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **William Tell Bridge**: rare: 5 archived performances [16]
- **George Washington Story/banter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **China Cat jam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-02-07.137392.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 111 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd69-02-07.late.sbd.wiley.14471.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 62 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has fade-ins and fade-outs, which the reviewer considers unavoidable; Audio is heavily compressed, making EQ nearly impossible, and hiss is loud, though instruments and vocals are clear [4][6]
- **gd69-02-07.early.sbd.wiley.14472.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 49 min; rated 4.43/5 by 14 [3]. Said about its sound: Very good quality, with some old tape hiss; Audio is heavily compressed, making EQ nearly impossible, and hiss is loud, though instruments and vocals are clear [5][7]

## Around the show

- The Velvet Underground and The Fugs also appear on the bill [1]
- Reviewer lived in a commune on Ellesworth Ave near Spahr St. when the Dead played the Stanley Theatre in Pittsburgh [15]
- The early show is good, but the late show is usually better, as here [9]
- The early show is good, but the late show is usually better, as here [10]
- This Dark Star resembles the Live Dead version from 2/27 [14]
- The show holds its own against the blockbuster nights a couple of weeks later [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-02-07.137392.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: Soundboard > master cassette (recorded by Bear (Owsley) on a "Concord" cassette deck model unknown > Ampex 90-minute cassette > Restoration &… [1]. Also: Source copy came from Jim Wise; two pops were removed and a few partial dropouts repaired; The Love Light has a splice at 7:48 [1]
- **gd69-02-07.late.sbd.wiley.14471.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bear Owsley; transferred by Rob Eaton, T. Wiley, and Jim Wise; source: Soundboard - Late Show [2]. Also: The master was a cassette rather than a reel tape [6]
- **gd69-02-07.early.sbd.wiley.14472.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bear Owsley; transferred by Rob Eaton, T. Wiley, and Jim Wise; source: Soundboard - Early Show [3]. Also: The master was a cassette rather than a reel tape [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Stanley Theatre, Pittsburgh Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/photos/stanley-theatre-pittsburgh-poster) [21]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Stanley Theatre - February 7, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/february-7-1969) [22]
